ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=49a7631b1ddb ('Profiling with firepit') introduced a database profiling setup script (scripts/db/reset_pg_statistics.sql) that executed TRUNCATE pg_statistic on the checkout-db PostgreSQL instance as part of profiling initialization. This wiped all table statistics for the orders table at 2026-05-16T11:57:44Z. Without statistics, the PostgreSQL query planner lost knowledge of column cardinality and value distributions for orders(status, user_id, created_at), causing it to abandon the existing idx_orders_user_status index and fall back to a full sequential scan across ~2.2 million rows. The fetch_user_orders query latency escalated from ~140ms to over 5 seconds, exhausting the 20-connection pool and triggering the circuit breaker, resulting in 503 responses for all checkout and cart endpoints.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately run ANALYZE orders; on checkout-db to rebuild pg_statistic rows — this takes under 60 seconds and will allow the planner to resume using idx_orders_user_status, restoring sub-200ms query latency. 2. Reset the circuit breaker in checkout-service by restarting the pod or calling the internal /admin/circuit-breaker/reset endpoint to allow traffic to resume. 3. Revert or patch commit 49a7631b1ddb to remove or gate the TRUNCATE pg_statistic call in reset_pg_statistics.sql behind an explicit DBA confirmation flag to prevent recurrence. 4. Add a post-deploy canary check that verifies pg_statistic row count for critical tables is non-zero before completing any deploy that touches db/maintenance scripts.
